question: My work permit was granted in February 2026. I am registering my application to extend it with Migrationsverket this week. What salary do I need for the extension?
reference_answer: Because the permit was granted before 1 June 2026 and the extension is registered with Migrationsverket by 1 December 2026, the older wording of 6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen applies (transitional provision 2 to SFS 2026:295; the same for the ordinance in SFS 2026:605): the employment must give good maintenance (god försörjning), which the ordinance (5 kap. 8 a § utlänningsförordningen in its older wording) defined as a salary of at least 80 percent of the median salary published by Statistics Sweden; Migrationsverket states this as at least SEK 30,640 a month before tax. 1 December 2026 is the last registration date: an extension registered from 2 December falls under the new requirement of at least 90 percent of the median salary. Salary, insurance and other terms must still be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice in the profession or industry.
notes: Version-dependent (phase 4 slice 4). Sources checked against the stored wordings and transitional provisions. Reference answer aligned 2026-11-24 with the reviewed multi-transition-salary-904 (review on the review page).

question: My work permit was granted in February 2026. I will apply to extend it in January 2027. What salary will I need?
reference_answer: The current rule applies: the salary must be at least 90 percent of the median salary in Sweden at the time of application (6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen, as amended by SFS 2026:295 from 1 June 2026). The older 80 percent rule under the transitional provisions applies only to extensions of permits granted before 1 June 2026 that are registered by 1 December 2026, and an application in January 2027 is registered too late. Salary, insurance and other terms must also be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice.
notes: Version-dependent (phase 4 slice 4). Sources checked against the stored wordings and transitional provisions.

question: I have a work permit in Sweden and want to extend it. What salary do I need?
reference_answer: It depends on when the permit was granted and when the extension is registered. If the permit was granted before 1 June 2026 and the extension is registered with Migrationsverket by 1 December 2026, the older rule applies: a salary of at least 80 percent of the median salary (god försörjning; transitional provision 2 to SFS 2026:295, ordinance 5 kap. 8 a § in its older wording). Otherwise the current rule applies: at least 90 percent of the median salary in Sweden at the time of application (6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen). In both cases salary, insurance and other terms must be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice.
notes: D8 vs answer rule 5: the expected kind (answer both branches vs ask for the dates) is the slice 4 decision; drafted as answered with both branches.

question: What salary do I need to get a Swedish work permit?
reference_answer: As of 1 June 2024: the employment must make it possible to achieve good maintenance (god försörjning) (6 kap. 2 § första stycket 1 utlänningslagen, wording of SFS 2022:1847), which the ordinance defines as a salary of at least 80 percent of the median salary published by Statistics Sweden, using the latest published median salary on the day the application came in (5 kap. 8 a § utlänningsförordningen, SFS 2023:570). Salary, insurance and other terms must be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice in the occupation or industry.
notes: Historical: the 90 percent rule only applies from 2026-06-01.

question: What salary is required for an EU Blue Card in Sweden?
reference_answer: As of 1 June 2024: the salary must be at least one and a half times the average gross annual salary in Sweden (6 a kap. 1 § utlänningslagen, wording of SFS 2013:606). The salary, insurance and other terms must also be no worse than Swedish collective agreements or practice.
notes: Historical: rebuilt 2013:606 wording (slice 3). The later threshold of 1.25 times (SFS 2024:1220, issued December 2024, in force 2025-01-01) did not exist on 2024-06-01: mentioning it is not required.
